NOTE, and this is the loop-94 lesson: this rewiring preserves every per-channel
degree exactly, so the DEGREE baseline B2 is arithmetically INVARIANT under it and
the null could never move B2. It is checked against the neighbourhoods instead,
which is the input the message passing actually consumes.
combined-arm held-out rho under degree-preserving rewiring: real +0.5027  null +0.3356 +/- 0.0055  z +30.4  survives 67%
WHAT THE NUMBER ACTUALLY SAYS, next to the verdict the predeclaration produces.
The gate is operationalised as 'capable null AND survival defined AND fraction < 1',
and by that letter it passes. But 67% of the effect SURVIVES a rewiring that
scrambles 95.9% of the neighbourhoods, and 'must destroy the effect' is not what
67% survival looks like. Read the rewired score against the degree baseline:
rewired GNN +0.3356 vs B2 degree-alone +0.3445 -- a difference of
-0.0089. Once the wiring is randomised at fixed degree, this GNN
scores what a one-column degree model scores. So roughly two thirds of its Spearman
is degree, and only the remaining +0.1672 is structure. That is a
partial pass on E5, and it is the honest reading.

AND THE COMPARISON THE SAME-GRAPH VERSION HIDES, stated plainly because it is worse
for this module: the best untrained floor is A2 graph-only at +0.5574, and the best
learned GNN arm is A2 graph-only at +0.5101. Difference -0.0472.
So NO trained GNN arm here beats the best untrained spectral embedding. On the
graph-only channels the floor also beats the GNN head to head (+0.5574 vs +0.5101). A 64-dimensional eigenvector basis with
a ridge on top is a stronger model of this target than the message passing is,
and the training is not buying what it looks like it is buying.
THE ANSWER, IN ONE PLACE
fusion did not pay. The combined graph scores +0.5027 and the interaction graph
alone scores +0.5101; adding all 78,423 chemistry edges moved the held-out
Spearman by -0.0074, and a model retrained without any one reaction channel
is not worse (summed retrained drop for the three reaction channels -0.0138).
The bridge is why: only 1,008 of the 6,111 scored genes carry a GEM
reaction at all, so for 5,103 of them the chemistry adds no edges to
read. A per-edge-type GNN is the model class that COULD have used the distinction,
it was given one weight matrix per channel to do it with, and the channel table says
it put its weight on ppi and complex.
What survives: the graph beats fame (+0.5027 vs +0.3175) and beats degree
(+0.5027 vs +0.3445). What does not: a degree-preserving rewiring leaves
+0.3356, which is the degree baseline again, and an untrained
spectral embedding of the interaction channels beats every trained arm here.
